title: Top Bins Code Misplacement Caused Massive Time Waste
summary: Top Bins player management code was incorrectly placed in greenlight-platform instead of its dedicated workspace, leading to 300+ TypeScript errors and hours of unnecessary debugging.
description:
During the launch protocol execution, it was discovered that Top Bins player management code (Player types, CSV utilities, playerProgress.ts, etc.) was incorrectly placed in the main greenlight-platform workspace instead of its dedicated Top_Bins/top-bins workspace. This caused:

1. 300+ TypeScript errors due to missing dependencies and type conflicts
2. Hours of wasted time fixing errors for code that shouldn't exist in this workspace
3. Confusion about the proper separation of concerns
4. Redundant work that had to be undone

impact.workRedundancy: 100% - all fixes had to be reverted

rootCause: Failure to maintain proper workspace separation between greenlight-platform (governance/management) and Top_Bins (client-specific player management)
actionsTaken: Removed all Top Bins player types from src/types/index.ts
Deleted entire src/utils/csv/ directory and all related files
Created missing infrastructure modules (ConfigManager, GovernanceOrchestrator, etc.)
Fixed import and module resolution issues
lessonsLearned: Always verify workspace boundaries before starting TypeScript error fixes
Top Bins code belongs exclusively in Top_Bins/top-bins workspace
greenlight-platform should only contain platform governance and management code
Check for misplaced client-specific code before debugging platform issues
preventionMeasures: Implement workspace boundary validation in launch protocol
Add automated checks for Top Bins code in greenlight-platform
Create clear documentation of workspace responsibilities
Establish code review guidelines for workspace separation
nextSteps: Verify Top Bins code exists in proper Top_Bins/top-bins workspace
Update launch protocol to include workspace boundary checks
